# @harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support

[![CI](https://github.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://github.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support/blob/main/LICENSE)
[![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-v2%20%7C%20v1%20%E2%89%A51.18.29-0ea5e9)](#compatibility)
[![Claude Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20Code-plugins%20compatible-7c3aed)](#compatibility)
[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.x-3178C6?logo=typescript&logoColor=white)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)

Loads **Claude Code plugins** and **[Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org)** packages into OpenCode as native skills, slash commands, subagents, MCP servers, instructions, and lifecycle hooks. Plugin files stay where they are; nothing is copied into `.opencode/` or `~/.agents/skills`.

Unrelated to the former unscoped npm package `opencode-claude-plugins`.

## Quickstart

1. **Tell it where your plugins are.** Either:

   **a. Config file** (recommended). Point straight at Claude's plugin directory, no symlink:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.agents
   cat > ~/.agents/agent-plugin-support.json <<'JSON'
   {
     "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support/main/schema/agent-plugin-support.schema.json",
     "sources": [
       { "path": "~/.claude/plugins", "format": "claude" }
     ]
   }
   JSON
   ```

   **b. Zero config.** With no config file, plugins are read from `~/.agents/plugins`, same layout as `~/.claude/plugins`. Symlink it:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.agents
   ln -s ~/.claude/plugins ~/.agents/plugins
   ```

   Codex also uses `~/.agents/plugins/` for its own plugin files; if you share that directory, prefer the config file and name each tool's directory explicitly.

2. **Add this package** to `opencode.json` (`plugins`, not `plugin`):

   ```json
   {
     "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
     "plugins": ["@harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support"]
   }
   ```

3. **Restart OpenCode** (`opencode service restart` if a background service is running).

Check what was found with `npx @harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support list` (plugins) and `... sources` (effective config).

### From git (local directory)

v2 only loads `index.js` / `index.ts` at the **folder root**. It ignores `package.json` `"main"`, and a path to a file is rejected.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support.git
cd opencode-agent-plugin-support
npm install
npm run build
```

```json
{
  "plugins": ["/absolute/path/to/opencode-agent-plugin-support"]
}
```

Restart OpenCode. Do **not** point `plugins` at `dist/index.js` or `src/index.ts`.

## Configuration

`~/.agents/agent-plugin-support.json` (user) and `<repo>/.agents/agent-plugin-support.json` (project). Both are optional; a JSON schema is at [`schema/agent-plugin-support.schema.json`](schema/agent-plugin-support.schema.json).

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support/main/schema/agent-plugin-support.schema.json",
  "sources": [
    { "path": "~/.claude/plugins", "format": "claude" },
    { "path": "~/.agents/plugins", "format": "agent-plugins" }
  ],
  "enabledPlugins": { "oh-my-claudecode@omc": false }
}
```

**`sources`**: directories to load plugins from, in priority order.

| Field | |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Directory. `~` is expanded; a relative path is relative to the config file's directory. |
| `format` | `claude`, `agent-plugins`, or `auto` (default). See below. |
| `label` | Suffix of Agent Plugins ids (`<name>@<label>`). Default: the directory name, or its parent's name when the directory is called `plugins` (`~/.agents/plugins` becomes `agents`). |
| `enabled` | `false` switches a source off, for example in a project to turn off a user source. |

A bare string is shorthand for `{ "path": "...", "format": "auto" }`.

| `format` | What the directory is |
| --- | --- |
| `claude` | A Claude plugin tree: `installed_plugins.json`, `known_marketplaces.json`, `cache/`, `marketplaces/`; directory marketplaces are read in place. Exactly the 0.1.x behavior. |
| `agent-plugins` | A directory whose immediate children are Agent Plugins packages (a root `plugin.json` declaring an agent-plugins.org `$schema`). Children named `cache`, `data`, `marketplaces`, `repos`, or starting with `.` are skipped. |
| `auto` | Decides per plugin by its manifests: the registry in `installed_plugins.json` if there is one, plus every child directory with a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (Claude) or an Agent Plugins `plugin.json`. |

**Merging.** Project sources come first, then user sources; a project entry with the same resolved path as a user entry replaces it. If no config file declares `sources`, the default is one `claude` source at `~/.agents/plugins`. If two enabled plugins from different sources have the same name, the first source wins and a warning is logged.

**Plugin ids.** `claude` plugins keep `name@marketplace`. Agent Plugins packages are `<name>@<label>`, with `name` from `plugin.json`: `greeter@agents`, or whatever `label` you set. `list` prints every id.

### Enablement

Plugins are enabled unless set to `false`. Highest precedence first:

1. `<repo>/.agents/agent-plugin-support.json` `enabledPlugins`
2. `~/.agents/agent-plugin-support.json` `enabledPlugins`
3. `<repo>/.agents/plugins.json` (legacy)
4. `~/.agents/plugins.json` (legacy)

> **Deprecated:** `plugins.json` still works and is read at lower precedence, but new setups should use `agent-plugin-support.json`. `extraKnownMarketplaces` is still read from `plugins.json` only.

Claude's `~/.claude/settings.json` is not read.

### Where data lives

`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` (Claude format) and `${PLUGIN_DATA}` (Agent Plugins format) are both `~/.agents/plugins/data/<id with unsafe characters replaced by "-">/`, created on first use, whichever sources you configure. Plugin updates and source changes do not move it.

## Security

Hook commands (`type: "command"` in `hooks.json`) run as **your user**: full environment, project cwd, and a **30s default timeout** (`timeout` in `hooks.json` is seconds). They can run any shell you would.

- **PreToolUse timeout is fail-closed:** if that hook hits the timeout, the tool call is blocked. A hung “deny this command” hook must not fail open.
- **Other hook events** still do not block on timeout (the process is killed; OpenCode continues). Exit `2` / JSON `deny` still block where those events support it.

Malformed `installed_plugins.json`, `plugin.json`, `hooks.json`, `.mcp.json`, `mcp.json`, config files, or YAML frontmatter are skipped with a warning; other plugins keep loading. A repo can declare `sources` in `<repo>/.agents/agent-plugin-support.json`, so only open repositories you trust (the same is true of OpenCode's own project config).

See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support/blob/main/SECURITY.md) to report a vulnerability.

## Options and compatibility

Object form (npm package; local directory+options is dropped on OpenCode **2.0.24**):

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support",
      "options": {
        "extraPluginDirs": { "my-plugin@local": "/path/to/claude-plugin" },
        "skipInstalled": false,
        "mcpDisabled": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

`extraPluginDirs` loads extra plugin directories (Claude or Agent Plugins, detected from the manifests) without writing a registry. `skipInstalled` skips discovery from every configured source. Prefer `install-local` (or that registry file) for Claude plugins if you need options on a local checkout.

### OpenCode v1

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["@harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support"]
}
```

Needs OpenCode **1.18.29+** (object entrypoint with `server()`).

### Compatibility

OpenCode **v2** is the primary target. A v1 `server()` export remains for OpenCode 1.18.29+. v2 does not run v1 plugin implementations.

`install-local` **refuses** to write through a `~/.agents/plugins` → `~/.claude/plugins` symlink unless you pass `--write-claude-registry`.

## Claude plugin trees

```text
~/.agents/plugins/          (or any `claude` source)
  installed_plugins.json
  known_marketplaces.json
  marketplaces/<name>/
  cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/
  data/<plugin-id>/
```

Plugin roots are found the way Claude Code finds them: a relative-path plugin of a local (`directory` / `file`) marketplace is read in place from that marketplace; otherwise `installPath` from `installed_plugins.json` (`~` / `$HOME` expanded, relative paths resolved from the source directory), then `cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/`, then the marketplace clone's plugin `source`. Plugins that only exist in Claude's cache (`github`, `git-subdir`, `npm`, ... sources) cannot be rebuilt here; refresh them in Claude Code. Details in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).

Project-scoped installs for **other** repos are ignored. If several entries remain, the one whose directory exists wins.

## Agent Plugins

Supports [Agent Plugins **1.0.0**](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/spec/1.0.0.md) (the only published version): a root `plugin.json` with `"$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json"`, `skills/<dir>/SKILL.md`, and `mcp.json`. Schemas are recognized locally and never fetched. A `1.1.0` (working draft) or unknown `$schema` rejects the plugin with a clear reason, as the spec requires for unsupported versions.

OpenCode-specific commands, agents, hooks, and instructions go in the client extension `com.harnesstap.opencode/` (Claude-like layout) and/or `extensions["com.harnesstap.opencode"]` in `plugin.json`:

```text
my-plugin/
  plugin.json
  skills/greet/SKILL.md
  mcp.json
  com.harnesstap.opencode/
    commands/hello.md
    agents/helper.md
    hooks/hooks.json
    instructions.md
```

Hook commands get `PLUGIN_ROOT` and `PLUGIN_DATA` next to the `CLAUDE_*` variables, and `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` / `${PLUGIN_DATA}` are expanded in `hooks.json`.

A plugin with **both** a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and an Agent Plugins `plugin.json`: from a `claude` or `auto` source, Claude is primary and the Agent Plugins `mcp.json` servers are added (a server name Claude already defines keeps the Claude definition; a differing `name` logs a warning and the Claude name stays the prefix). From an `agent-plugins` source, only the Agent Plugins side is read. An invalid Agent Plugins manifest on such a plugin falls back to Claude with a warning.

## CLI

Bin name: `opencode-agent-plugin-support`.

```bash
npx @harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support list
npx @harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support sources
npx @harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support enable name@marketplace
npx @harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support disable name@marketplace --project
npx @harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support install-local ./my-claude-plugin [name@local]
npx @harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support install-local ./my-claude-plugin --write-claude-registry
npx @harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support marketplace-add my-market github:org/repo
```

After a global install, the same commands work as `opencode-agent-plugin-support …`.

- `list` — every plugin with effective on/off and where that was decided (`source`: `default` | `user` | `project`, plus `sourceFile`), the `format` it was loaded as (`claude` | `agent-plugins`), its configured source (`sourcePath`, `sourceLabel`, `sourceFormat`), `dualManifest`, the resolved `root`, how it was found (`resolvedVia`), every location tried (`tried`), `reason` when it is off or unresolved, MCP servers left out (`mcpSkipped`), and `diagnostics`.
- `sources` (alias `config`) — the effective config: which config files exist, the merged sources with labels and origin, and every `enabledPlugins` key with the file that decides it. Reads config only; it does not load plugins. Set `OPENCODE_AGENT_PLUGIN_SUPPORT_DEBUG=1` to log resolution to stderr.
- `enable` / `disable` — write `agent-plugin-support.json` in the user directory (or the repo with `--project`) when that file exists, otherwise the legacy `plugins.json`. Other fields of the file are kept.
- `install-local` — register a local directory in `~/.agents/plugins` (must exist). Does not clone git marketplaces. Prints a note if `~/.agents/plugins` is not one of your sources.
- `marketplace-add` — record an extra marketplace (`github:org/repo` or a path).

## Support

| Component | OpenCode v2 | OpenCode v1 | Claude format | Agent Plugins format |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skills | `ctx.skill.transform` | `config.skills.paths` | `skills/**/SKILL.md`, manifest `skills` paths, root `SKILL.md`. Lenient frontmatter. Invocable as `/plugin:skill`; `user-invocable: false` skips the command, `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps the command but hides the skill from the model. | Immediate children `skills/<dir>/SKILL.md` only, validated as [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/specification) (name equals the directory, description required); an invalid skill is skipped, siblings load. |
| MCP | `ctx.mcp.transform` (`disabled`) | `config.mcp` (`enabled`) | `.mcp.json` / manifest `mcpServers`. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` / `_DATA` / `_PROJECT_DIR` / `$ENV` expanded. stdio, `url` / `http` / `sse` / `ws` (all mapped to local / remote). | Root `mcp.json`, strict 1.0.0 rules. `stdio` and `streamable-http` run; `sse` is skipped with a report (OpenCode has no SSE client). Only `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` / `${PLUGIN_DATA}` expand; `PLUGIN_ROOT` / `PLUGIN_DATA` are set in the server's environment. An invalid entry skips that server, a bad file disables MCP for that plugin. |
| Commands | `ctx.command.transform` | `config.command` | `commands/**/*.md` and manifest `commands`, namespaced `plugin:command`. `$ARGUMENTS` works. | From `com.harnesstap.opencode/commands/` or `extensions`, namespaced with the plugin `name`. |
| Instructions | re-injected on every `session.context` | `config.instructions` + system transform | Plugin-root `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `INSTRUCTIONS.md`. | Only `com.harnesstap.opencode/instructions.md`. Root `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` are not injected. |
| Agents | `ctx.agent.transform` `update()` (inserts if missing) | `config.agent` | `agents/**/*.md`, namespaced `plugin:agent`, `mode: "subagent"`. | From `com.harnesstap.opencode/agents/` or `extensions`. |
| Hooks | tool / session / permission / event subscribe | v1 hook object | `hooks/hooks.json`, command hooks (`type: "command"`) only. | `com.harnesstap.opencode/hooks/hooks.json` or inline, same event support. `PLUGIN_ROOT` / `PLUGIN_DATA` set. |
| `bin/` on `PATH` | `shell.hook("create.before")` | `shell.env` | Yes. | No. |

Every file an Agent Plugins package supplies must resolve (symlinks followed) inside the plugin root: `plugin.json`, `skills/`, each `SKILL.md`, MCP `command` and `cwd`, and extension files.

**Hooks wired on v2:** PreToolUse (block + `updatedInput`), PostToolUse / PostToolUseFailure (`additionalContext`), UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart (matcher = `startup` / `clear` / `compact`), SessionEnd, Stop (`session.idle`), PermissionRequest (`permission.evaluate`), PreCompact (`session.compaction`).

**Not loaded:** LSP, output styles, themes, monitors, workflows, in-process JS mods, `.mcpb` bundles, HTTP/prompt/MCP/agent hooks, and most other Claude hook events.

Skill **ids** stay kebab-case (OpenCode cannot namespace them as `plugin:name`). Invoke a plugin skill with `/plugin:skill` even if a user skill shares the name. Commands, agents, and MCP **are** namespaced as `plugin:component`.

v2 built-in tool ids `shell`, `patch`, and `subagent` map to Claude `Bash`, `Edit`, and `Task` for hook matchers.

This OpenCode plugin’s `id` is `opencode-agent-plugin-support`.

## License

MIT

How injection works: [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md). Development: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

# Architecture

Runtime bridge: Claude Code plugin trees and Agent Plugins packages stay on disk where they are (by default `~/.agents/plugins/`, same layout as `~/.claude/plugins/`; any directory via `sources`). This package never copies components into `.opencode/` or `~/.agents/skills`.

OpenCode **v2** is the primary host. The default export is `{ id, setup, server }`:

- v2 reads `id` + `setup(ctx)` and ignores `server()`. There is no `config` hook; plugins register through domain `transform` / `hook` APIs.
- v1 (1.18.29+) calls `server()`, which is the original function plugin (`createClaudeCodeBridge`).

A root `index.js` re-exports `./dist/index.js` so a **directory** path in v2 `plugins` loads (v2 does not honor `package.json` `"main"` for local folders, and rejects file paths).

## Config and sources

`src/config.ts` reads `~/.agents/agent-plugin-support.json` and `<cwd>/.agents/agent-plugin-support.json` (`parseConfigDocument` is pure; problems are warnings, never fatal) and `mergeConfigLayers` produces the effective source list:

- Neither file declares `sources` → one implicit source `{ path: ~/.agents/plugins, format: claude }`. Together with the legacy `plugins.json` precedence below this is exactly 0.1.x.
- Otherwise project sources first, then user sources, deduplicated by resolved path (project wins, which is also how `enabled: false` removes a user source). `~` is expanded and relative paths resolve from the declaring file's directory.
- Labels (the `@<label>` of Agent Plugins ids) are explicit or derived (`deriveSourceLabel`) and made unique with a `-2` suffix and a warning.

Enablement (`src/enablement.ts`) resolves a key through four layers, first hit wins: project config, user config, project `plugins.json`, user `plugins.json`. `enable` / `disable` write the layer's config file when it exists (other fields preserved, refused if it is not valid JSON), else the legacy file.

`discoverEnabledPlugins` (`src/discover.ts`) walks the sources in order through `src/source-discovery.ts`, then drops a plugin whose **name** (the namespace prefix) was already provided by an earlier source. Duplicates inside one source keep 0.1.x behavior. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` / `${PLUGIN_DATA}` is always `~/.agents/plugins/data/<slug>`, independent of sources (`pluginDataDir` ignores `RuntimePaths.storeDir`).

| Source format | What `source-discovery` does |
| --- | --- |
| `claude` | Registry readers with `RuntimePaths.storeDir` set to the source (the steps under **Discovery**). |
| `agent-plugins` | Sorted immediate children, skipping `cache`, `data`, `marketplaces`, `repos`, dot-directories and non-directories. Each child's `realpath` is the plugin root; root `plugin.json` decides. |
| `auto` | Registry (if present) and children. Per plugin: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` → Claude (plus dual merge); else an Agent Plugins `plugin.json` → Agent Plugins; else ignored. For a registry plugin without a Claude manifest but with a valid Agent Plugins one, Agent Plugins semantics apply and the registry id is kept. |

## Agent Plugins loading (1.0.0)

Modules: `ap-manifest.ts` (manifest), `ap-skills.ts`, `ap-mcp.ts`, `ap-extension.ts` (`com.harnesstap.opencode`), `safe-path.ts` (containment), `plugin-build.ts` (assembly).

- **Version.** `$schema` must equal the 1.0.0 identifier. `1.1.0` is a working draft whose schemas differ only in `$id`/`$schema`; it is rejected like any unsupported version, because the spec only allows accepting identifiers a client explicitly recognizes as compatible. Schemas are never fetched.
- **Manifest** (§5): closed field set; unknown top-level fields and a non-object `extensions` are reported and ignored; everything else (including the name rule: 1-64 of `a-z0-9.-`, alphanumeric ends, no `--` or `..`) rejects the plugin. Contents of other clients' `extensions` namespaces are not validated.
- **Containment** (§4.1). `resolveWithin(realBase, target)` requires the lexical path and the symlink-resolved path (nearest existing ancestor, plus the missing tail) to stay inside the base; a dangling or looping link is refused. Applied to `plugin.json` (rejects the plugin), `skills/` (disables skills), each `SKILL.md` (skips it), MCP `command` and `cwd` (skips the server; `${PLUGIN_DATA}`-rooted `cwd` is checked against the data directory) and extension files.
- **Skills** (§7.1). Immediate children of `skills/` with a `SKILL.md` regular file; no recursion. Frontmatter is checked against the Agent Skills spec (name format and equal to the directory, description 1-1024, optional field types); extra fields are tolerated. Invalid skills are skipped and reported.
- **MCP** (§7.2, §9). `loadAgentMcp` validates `mcp.json` (closed top-level, `$schema` equal to the plugin's version), then each entry: closed variants `stdio` / `streamable-http` / `sse`; `command` is one token (bare name or `./` path, never expanded, resolved against the plugin root, not `cwd`); `cwd` must be `./…`, `${PLUGIN_ROOT}…` or `${PLUGIN_DATA}…`; URL must be absolute http(s) without userinfo or fragment, https unless `localhost` or a loopback IP literal; header names are RFC 9110 tokens, no case-folded duplicates, values without control characters; `env` may not define `PLUGIN_ROOT` / `PLUGIN_DATA`. Expansion is one regex pass over `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` / `${PLUGIN_DATA}` in `args`, `env` values and `cwd` only. The two variables are set in the environment after `env`. A valid `sse` entry is skipped as unsupported (OpenCode has no SSE client). Mapping: stdio → `local` (`command`, `environment`, `cwd`), `streamable-http` → `remote`.
- **No Claude extras.** Root `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` are not injected and `bin/` is not put on `PATH`.
- **OpenCode extension.** `ap-extension.ts` runs the Claude loaders with `com.harnesstap.opencode/` as the base (default `commands/`, `agents/`, `hooks/hooks.json`; only `instructions.md` for instructions) and with inline `commands`, `agents`, `hooks` from `extensions["com.harnesstap.opencode"]`. Unlike a Claude manifest, inline declarations add to the default directories instead of replacing them. A file filter (`FileFilter`) applies containment to every file read. Hook processes get `PLUGIN_ROOT` / `PLUGIN_DATA` (`hookEnv`, `agentPluginsRoot`), and `expandString` expands both names (`ExpandContext.pluginVars`).
- **Reporting.** Everything the spec says to report goes through `Diagnostics`: logged as a warning (debug for disabled plugins) and kept in `EnabledPlugin.diagnostics`, shown by `list`. Skipped MCP servers are in `mcpSkipped`.

### Dual manifests

A plugin with a valid Agent Plugins `plugin.json` (the `$schema` identifies it; a root `plugin.json` without an agent-plugins.org `$schema` is ignored) in a `claude` or `auto` source (or with a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` in `auto`) is loaded Claude-first (`hydrateClaudePlugin`) and `mcp.json` servers are added when the Claude manifest does not already define the name. The Claude name stays the namespace prefix and a different Agent Plugins `name` warns. Skills, commands, agents, instructions, hooks and `bin/` come from the Claude layout only. An invalid or unsupported Agent Plugins manifest warns and the plugin is Claude-only. In an `agent-plugins` source only the Agent Plugins side exists.

## Discovery

1. Read activation from the four enablement layers (see **Config and sources**). Missing file/key → enabled. Manifest `defaultEnabled` is ignored. Everything below applies per `claude` source, with `~/.agents/plugins` standing for the source directory.
2. Parse `<source>/installed_plugins.json` (see versions below). Optional v2/v1 plugin option `skipInstalled` skips this.
3. For each record, pick an installation:
   - Drop `project` / `local` entries whose `projectPath` is a different cwd.
   - Rank remaining: matching-cwd `local` / `project`, then other `local` / `project` without a foreign path, then `user`, `managed`.
   - Prefer the best-ranked entry whose directory exists.
4. Resolve the plugin root (`src/plugin-root.ts`), first hit wins. This mirrors Claude Code, which loads relative-path plugins of local marketplaces in place and copies everything else into `cache/`, and sweeps cache dirs it no longer uses:
   1. **Local marketplace, in place.** If the plugin's marketplace is a `directory` / `file` marketplace (`known_marketplaces.json` `installLocation` or `source.path`, or `extraKnownMarketplaces` in `plugins.json`) and the `marketplace.json` entry has a relative-path `source`, use that directory. It wins over a cache copy because Claude reads it live.
   2. `installPath` (`~` / `$HOME` expanded). Relative paths are resolved from the source directory (not `$HOME`), so Claude’s `cache/...` values work.
   3. `cache/<marketplace>/<name>/<version>/`.
   4. **Marketplace tree.** For git-hosted marketplaces, the clone (`installLocation`, `marketplaces/<name>/`, `marketplaces/<repo-slug>/`, or the `marketplaces/<name>.json` file of a `url` marketplace) plus the entry's relative `source`.

   Relative `source` rules (`src/marketplace.ts`): resolved from the marketplace root (the directory containing `.claude-plugin/`); `"."` is the root; a bare name resolves under `metadata.pluginRoot`; `..`, backslashes, and escapes are refused. Object sources (`github`, `url`, `git-subdir`, `npm`, `archive`, `command`) are never resolved from a marketplace tree because only Claude’s cache has them; fetching is Claude’s job.

   When nothing resolves, the plugin is skipped with `plugin root unresolved: ...` listing each place tried. That is logged with `warn` for enabled plugins (`debug` for disabled ones) and shown by `list` (`reason`, `resolvedVia`, `tried`). `OPENCODE_AGENT_PLUGIN_SUPPORT_DEBUG=1` also logs successful resolutions to stderr.
5. For `installPath` / cache hits, find the plugin root (directory containing `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` or equivalent; marketplace hits are already exact). Load the manifest and merge the marketplace entry (`src/marketplace-entry.ts`): no `plugin.json` → the entry is the manifest; `strict` (default `true`) → the entry's `commands` / `agents` / `skills` / `hooks` are appended (hooks are appended, not replaced per event); `strict: false` with entry components → "Plugin has conflicting manifests"; an entry at the marketplace root (`"."`) that lists `skills` replaces the default `skills/` scan; display fields come from the entry, `version` from the manifest. Then hydrate skills / commands / agents / MCP / instructions / hooks.
6. Plugin option `extraPluginDirs` (`{ id: "/abs/path" }`) appends more trees without a registry write.

`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` maps to `~/.agents/plugins/data/<slug>/` (fixed, whatever the sources) and that directory is created on first use. Plugin `bin/` is prepended onto `PATH` (v1 `shell.env`, v2 `ctx.shell.hook("create.before")`) while the plugin is enabled.

Malformed `installed_plugins.json`, a plugin's `plugin.json`, `hooks.json`, `.mcp.json`, or YAML frontmatter is skipped with a warning; other plugins and components still load. The OpenCode plugin `id` is `opencode-agent-plugin-support`.

Duplicate `SKILL.md` paths (manifest `skills` overlapping default `skills/`) are skipped.

## Config injection

### v2 (`setup`)

v2 has no mutable global config object.

| Claude component | v2 API | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skills/*/SKILL.md` | `ctx.skill.transform` `editor.add` | `{ id, name, description?, path, content }`. Not namespaced (kebab-case only). Skipped when `disable-model-invocation` is set. Also registered as `/plugin:skill` commands (see Commands). |
| `commands/*.md` | `ctx.command.transform` `editor.add` | Native slash commands, plus user-invocable plugin skills as `plugin:skill`. Executor substitutes `$ARGUMENTS` and calls `ctx.session.prompt`. |
| `agents/*.md` | `ctx.agent.transform` | See **Agents** below. |
| `.mcp.json` / `mcpServers` (Claude) or `mcp.json` (Agent Plugins) | `ctx.mcp.transform` `editor.set` | Native MCP. v2 field is `disabled` (not `enabled`). |
| `CLAUDE.md` / … | `ctx.session.hook("context")` | Push instruction texts onto `event.system` **every** model call (v2 context is not persisted). |
| `hooks/hooks.json` | session / tool / permission hooks + `ctx.event.subscribe` | Command hooks only. |
| `bin/` | `ctx.shell.hook("create.before")` | Prepend `PATH`. |

### v1 (`config` hook)

The `config` hook runs at plugin init and mutates the live config object:

| Claude component | OpenCode field | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skills/*/SKILL.md` | `config.skills.paths` (or `config.skills` if it is already a string array) | Same discovery as `.agents/skills`. Paths omitted for `disable-model-invocation` skills. |
| `commands/*.md` | `config.command["plugin:name"]` | Native slash commands, plus `plugin:skill` for each user-invocable plugin skill. |
| `agents/*.md` | `config.agent["plugin:name"]` | `mode: "subagent"`. |
| `.mcp.json` / `mcpServers` | `config.mcp["plugin:name"]` | Native MCP (`type: local \| remote`, `enabled`). |
| `CLAUDE.md` / … | `config.instructions` + `experimental.chat.system.transform` | File paths plus inlined text. |
| `hooks/hooks.json` | mapped plugin hooks | Command hooks only. |
| `bin/` | `shell.env` `PATH` | Prepended while enabled. |

Skill **ids** stay the `SKILL.md` folder names (OpenCode skill ids cannot contain `:`). Each user-invocable plugin skill is also a slash command named `plugin:skill` (for example `/code-review-workflow:request-slack-review`). That command inlines the plugin file so a colliding user skill in `~/.config/opencode/skills` cannot replace it. If the plugin already defines a command with the same namespaced id, that command wins. Commands, agents, and MCP servers **are** namespaced as `plugin:component`.

### Component mapping details

- **Skills:** Frontmatter `name` + `description` are required by OpenCode. Search roots: `skills/`, manifest `skills` paths, or a root-level `SKILL.md`. Claude fields: `user-invocable` (default true; `false` skips the slash command), `disable-model-invocation` (keeps `/plugin:skill` but does not advertise the skill to the model), `argument-hint` (copied onto the command), `when_to_use` (appended to the listing description). Boolean frontmatter accepts Claude's `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off`/`1`/`0`. If frontmatter `name` already starts with `plugin:`, the prefix is not doubled.
- **MCP:** `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`, `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`, and `$ENV` expanded. stdio / `command` → `type: "local"`; `url` / `http` / `sse` / `ws` → `type: "remote"`. `.mcpb` bundles are not unpacked. `${user_config.*}` expands only when `userConfig` is passed in.
- **Commands:** Markdown files plus inline `plugin.json` maps, then plugin skills as `/plugin:skill`. `$ARGUMENTS` is preserved. Skill-command templates include the plugin `SKILL.md` path and body (and expand `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` / `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`).
- **Instructions:** Claude itself does **not** load plugin-root `CLAUDE.md`; we still do because it is the natural OpenCode mapping.
- **Agents (v1):** `description`; `tools` / `disallowedTools` → OpenCode `tools` booleans; `model` aliases (`haiku` / `sonnet` / `opus`) or `provider/model`. Plugin-agent `hooks` / `mcpServers` / `permissionMode` ignored.

### Agents on v2

Published plugin docs expose `AgentEditor` as `list` / `get` / `default` / `update` / `remove` (no `add` on OpenCode 2.0.24). Upstream `packages/core/src/agent.ts` implements `update` as **insert-on-miss** (`Info.empty(id)` then the callback). That is the legitimate way to register Claude plugin subagents without copying markdown into `~/.config/opencode` or `.opencode/`.

If a future host adds `editor.add`, we call it first and fall back to `update`.

`Agent.Info` uses `system` (not `prompt`) and `permissions` (not v1 `tools` booleans). We set `mode: "subagent"`, `hidden: false`, `system` from the agent markdown, optional `{ providerID, id }` model. Claude tool allowlists are not rewritten into v2 permission rulesets (lossy; would be a silent policy change).

We do **not** copy agent files into user directories.

## Hook execution

Only `type: "command"` hooks run (HTTP, prompt, MCP, and agent hooks are skipped). Matchers (`Bash`, `Write|Edit`) are compared against **Claude** tool names. OpenCode v1 `bash` / `edit` / `write` and v2 `shell` / `patch` / `subagent` (and related) are translated first.

Plugin MCP tool ids on v2 look like `fixture-demo_echo-api_echo` and map to Claude `mcp__plugin_fixture-demo_echo-api__echo` when the namespaced server `fixture-demo:echo-api` is known.

**SessionStart / SessionEnd / PreCompact** matchers are session sources (`startup`, `clear`, `auto` / `manual`), not tool names. Passing no matcher name still skips groups that declare a matcher.

Processes get Claude-style stdin JSON (`hook_event_name`, `session_id`, `cwd`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, …) and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` / `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` / `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` in the environment. Timeout defaults to 30s (`hooks.json` `timeout` is seconds). If `args` is empty, the command string is run via the shell. A **PreToolUse** timeout fails closed (the tool call is blocked). Other hook events do not treat timeout as a block.

Stdout is parsed as JSON when possible (`hookSpecificOutput`, `decision`, `additionalContext`, `updatedInput`, `continue`). Interpretation:

- Exit `2`, `permissionDecision: "deny"`, `decision: "block"`, or `continue: false` → block.
- `updatedInput` merges into tool args (PreToolUse).
- `additionalContext` is appended to tool output, prompt text, or compacting context depending on the event.
- PostToolUse vs PostToolUseFailure: v1 uses empty/error-like output; v2 uses `event.status === "error"`.

UserPromptSubmit block replaces the prompt text (OpenCode has no first-class reject). SessionStart context is cached per session and re-injected on every v2 `context` hook (and queued into v1 `experimental.chat.system.transform`).

### Event mapping

| Claude event | v2 | v1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PreToolUse` | `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before")` | `tool.execute.before`, `permission.ask` |
| `PostToolUse` | `ctx.tool.hook("execute.after")` | `tool.execute.after` |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | `execute.after` when `status === "error"` | `tool.execute.after` (heuristic) |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | `ctx.session.hook("prompt")` | `chat.message` |
| `SessionStart` | `ctx.session.hook("context")` + `session.created` events; matcher `startup` | `event` `session.created`, first `chat.message` |
| `SessionEnd` | `ctx.event.subscribe` `session.deleted` / `session.removed`; matcher `clear` | `event` `session.deleted` |
| `Stop` | `session.idle` events | `event` `session.idle` |
| `PermissionRequest` | `ctx.permission.hook("evaluate")` | `permission.ask` |
| `PreCompact` | `ctx.session.hook("compaction")`; matcher `auto` / `manual` | `experimental.session.compacting` |

Unmapped (not executed): `Setup`, `UserPromptExpansion`, `PermissionDenied`, `PostToolBatch`, `Notification`, `MessageDisplay`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `TaskCreated`, `TaskCompleted`, `StopFailure`, `TeammateIdle`, `InstructionsLoaded`, `ConfigChange`, `CwdChanged`, `DirectoryAdded`, `FileChanged`, `WorktreeCreate`, `WorktreeRemove`, `PostCompact`, `PreModelSwitch`, `PostModelSwitch`, `Elicitation`, `ElicitationResult`.

## `installed_plugins.json` versions

Readers accept:

- **v1** object: `{ plugins: { "name@market": { installPath, … } } }`
- **v2** object: `{ version: 2, plugins: { "name@market": [entries] } }`
- **v3** array of entries (`id` / `plugin` / `name`+`marketplace` plus install fields)

`install-local` always writes **v2**. It refuses when `~/.agents/plugins` is Claude’s store (symlink / same realpath as `~/.claude/plugins`) unless `--write-claude-registry`. Multiple installations per id are kept; `pickInstallation` ranks by scope against the current cwd and prefers an existing directory. Writes replace the file with v2 (so a v1/v3 file becomes v2 after `install-local`).

## 0.1.1 - 2026-10-11

Fix plugins that Claude Code loads from their marketplace never showing up in OpenCode (for example a plugin in a `directory` marketplace whose `cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/` copy Claude had swept).

- Resolve the plugin root the way Claude Code does, in this order: relative-path plugin of a `directory` / `file` marketplace (loaded in place, never from the cache), then `installPath` (absolute, or relative to the plugins dir), then `cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/`, then the marketplace's own tree (`installLocation`, `marketplaces/<name>/`, `marketplaces/<name>.json`, or an `extraKnownMarketplaces` path) via the plugin entry's `source` in `marketplace.json`.
- Understand relative `source` strings (`./path`, `"."`, bare names under `metadata.pluginRoot`) and refuse `..`, backslashes, and paths that escape the marketplace. Object sources (`github`, `url`, `git-subdir`, `npm`, `archive`, `command`) only exist in Claude's cache, so they are reported as unresolved with a hint to refresh in Claude Code.
- Honor marketplace entries as manifests: an entry is the manifest when the plugin has no `plugin.json`; otherwise `strict` (default `true`) appends the entry's `commands` / `agents` / `skills` / `hooks`, and `strict: false` with entry components fails with "Plugin has conflicting manifests". Entry display fields override, manifest `version` wins.
- An unresolvable enabled plugin now logs a warning that lists every place tried (silent before). Set `OPENCODE_AGENT_PLUGIN_SUPPORT_DEBUG=1` for per-plugin resolution lines on stderr.
- `list` adds `resolvedVia` and `tried`, and `reason` now explains why a plugin is unresolved (`plugin root unresolved: ...`, replacing `installPath missing: ...`).

First public release of `@harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support` (OpenCode plugin id `opencode-agent-plugin-support`, CLI bin `opencode-agent-plugin-support`).

## Release (maintainers)

npm publish runs only in CI (`release.yml`), matching [harnesstap/harnesstap](https://github.com/harnesstap/harnesstap): GitHub-hosted runner, `permissions: id-token: write`, `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org`, then `npm publish --access public` **in this workflow file** (not `workflow_call`). Provenance is automatic with trusted publishing; the repo must be **public**.

### Cut a release

1. Bump `version` in `package.json` (keep it in lockstep with the git tag).
2. Add a matching heading in `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Merge to `main`, then tag and push:

   ```bash
   git tag v0.1.0
   git push origin v0.1.0
   ```

   Tag `v*` must equal `package.json` `version` (with or without the `v` prefix). The workflow fails if they differ, and skips publish if that version is already on npm.

4. Optional: **Actions → Release → Run workflow** (`workflow_dispatch`) and pass the tag.

Do not publish from a laptop except the one-time first publish below.

### One-time npm setup

The `@harnesstap` npm scope already exists (org/user `harnesstap`, maintainer `kayrnt`). Provenance requires this GitHub repository to be public.

**Trusted publisher (after the package exists on npm):** on [npmjs.com](https://www.npmjs.com/) → package `@harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support` → **Settings → Trusted publishing** → GitHub Actions:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Organization or user | `harnesstap` |
| Repository | `opencode-agent-plugin-support` |
| Workflow filename | `release.yml` (filename only, not a path) |
| Environment name | leave empty (this workflow does not use a GitHub Environment) |
| Allowed actions | allow **`npm publish`** |

Complete the first successful OIDC publish within **2 days** of creating that configuration, or npm expires it.

npm’s Trusted Publisher UI is on the **package** settings page. Current npm docs do not provide a PyPI-style pending publisher for a name that is not on the registry yet, so **the first publish cannot use OIDC until the package exists**.

**First publish of `0.1.0` (once):** as npm user `kayrnt`, from a clean `main` checkout at the tagged commit:

```bash
npm login   # kayrnt, with publish rights on @harnesstap
npm ci
npm publish --access public
```

Then add the trusted publisher table above. Later `v*` tags publish via OIDC with **no `NPM_TOKEN`**.

If you prefer the first publish to also run in GitHub Actions, temporarily uncomment the `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` block in `.github/workflows/release.yml`, add repo secret `NPM_TOKEN` (granular automation token with write to `@harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support`), push `v0.1.0`, then remove the secret and restore OIDC-only.

Enable [GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/security-advisories/working-with-repository-security-advisories/configuring-private-vulnerability-reporting-for-a-repository) on this repo (Settings → Code security).

# Security policy

## Supported versions

This package is in active development (`0.x`). Security fixes land on the latest release of `main`.

| Version | Supported |
| --- | --- |
| Latest `0.x` release | Yes |
| Older `0.x` releases | Best effort |
| Pre-release / development builds | No |

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Do not open a public GitHub issue for security vulnerabilities.**

Use [GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/harnesstap/opencode-agent-plugin-support/security/advisories/new) on this repository.

Repository owners: enable **Private vulnerability reporting** under GitHub **Settings → Code security and analysis** (or **Settings → Security**) if the advisory form is not available yet.

Include as much detail as you can: impact, reproduction steps, affected versions or commits, and logs or a proof of concept when it is safe to share.

We aim to acknowledge reports within **3 business days** and will work with you on a fix and coordinated disclosure.

## Scope

In scope: this npm package, its CLI, and GitHub Actions workflows in this repository.

Out of scope: third-party Claude Code plugins you load through this bridge (their hook commands run as your user; see the README Security section), OpenCode itself, and Claude Code.

## Safe disclosure

We appreciate responsible disclosure. We will credit reporters in release notes when they wish to be named.
